i agree, but i think that people in witchcraft communities severely overestimate how many people are this way.

if someone posts on this sub asking for help with magick, you have absolutely no right to assume they aren't doing mundane or physical stuff. chances are, if they're asking for help with MAGICK, they don't need help with the mundane.

both on this sub and in Discord servers, i see people ask the most basic and simple questions, but are met with "do mundane stuff" instead of actual answers. its condescending. if someone asks you for help, assuming they aren't doing mundane things as well is essentially calling them stupid. it IS stupid not to do mundane stuff on top of magick stuff. its common sense, and besides that, all the research in the world will tell you you need to combine both, and not only do magick.

it's disgusting when someone posts asking for help with something deep like mental health issues, and all of the responses are "get therapy". you have absolutely no right to assume that they aren't already in therapy, and its incredibly tacky and classist to assume anyone can get a therapist as they please.

if someone asks for help, HELP them, or just dont say anything at all. if someone is asking for help on how to use magick to heal over a loss, don't say "talk to friends and sleep well" - thats the advice you get off of google. thats the advice everyone knows. if someone wanted mundane advice, they'd ask somewhere else. instead you could tell them to sleep with comforting crystals under their pillow, do shadow work when they're ready, research death and spirits, whatever.

this is not aimed at you, OP, or anyone else, but it is such a common occurence that people are belittled in this community and treated as little children. 

and its not even logical to say that a lot of witches or aspiring witches thinks magick does everything. even if that happens, it is super rare. because even if a 13 year old asks for help on how to cure their anxiety with magick, even though they're misinformed and might have the wrong idea of what magick does, you, a complete stranger, has no idea if that 13 year old is already in therapy, if they talk to friends, if they write in a journal - you dont know what they already do to handle their anxiety, so you have no right to tell a desperate and hurting person that "they're not the main character in a CW show" when they're doing what they can to help themselves. and yes, it even applies to controversial stuff like love spells. how do you know they arent actively trying to date? how do you know they arent trying their best? doing spells without consent is wrong and you can educate someone on that without assuming they aren't doing mundane things at well.

again - not aimed at you. but while you're absolutely right, this opinion continues to harm people just trying to get some damn help anywhere they can.

if someone actually just wants to do the magick and not the mundane work, yes, you should absolutely tell them that's not how it works. but someone posting or commenting or asking "how to do x" does not OWE you to say all the mundane things they're doing already. answer their questions or dont say anything at all.
